# Skill sensitivity

Of all the tunable knobs, the **skill gate** — the correlation cutoff below which
we declare SEAS5 untrustworthy and withhold a forecast — moves the alert set the
most. This chapter quantifies that sensitivity. The cutoff is *chosen* in the next
chapter, by backtesting; here we just map the terrain.

The sweep driver is `skill_sweep.py`; it re-runs the pipeline at
r ∈ {0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35} and writes `../data/sweep/`. This chapter reads those
outputs, so it renders without Earth Engine.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

THRESHOLDS = [0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35]
TAGS = {r: "r%02d" % int(round(r * 100)) for r in THRESHOLDS}
adm0 = {r: pd.read_parquet(f"../data/sweep/adm0_{t}.parquet") for r, t in TAGS.items()}
KEY = ["admin", "season"]
```

## The gate dominates the analysed universe

```{python}
#| label: tbl-coverage
rows = []
for r in THRESHOLDS:
    d = adm0[r]
    ev = d[d.state == "evaluable"]
    rows.append(dict(r=r, evaluable=len(ev),
                     not_evaluable=(d.state == "not_evaluable_low_skill").sum(),
                     alert=(ev.tier == "alert").sum(),
                     watch=(ev.tier == "watch").sum()))
summary = pd.DataFrame(rows)
summary
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Evaluable (admin × season) rows and drought alerts rise sharply as the skill gate relaxes."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(summary.r, summary.evaluable, "o-", label="evaluable rows")
ax.plot(summary.r, summary.alert, "s-", label="alert")
ax.plot(summary.r, summary.watch, "^-", label="watch")
ax.set_xlabel("skill cutoff  (Spearman r)")
ax.set_ylabel("count (adm0, issued June 2026)")
ax.invert_xaxis()
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Relaxing 0.35 → 0.20 nearly **doubles** the evaluable set. Wherever we draw this
line dominates everything downstream — so it deserves a real criterion.

## A stable core, and a threshold-sensitive tail

If an alert fires regardless of the cutoff, it isn't an artefact of where the line
was drawn. We pivot every (admin × season) cell *ever* flagged `alert` and count how
many thresholds it survives.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-robustness
piv = None
for r in THRESHOLDS:
    s = adm0[r].set_index(KEY)["tier"].rename(TAGS[r])
    piv = s.to_frame() if piv is None else piv.join(s, how="outer")
piv = piv.fillna("not_eval")

is_alert = piv[list(TAGS.values())] == "alert"
ever = piv[is_alert.any(axis=1)].copy()
ever["n_thresh_alert"] = is_alert.loc[ever.index].sum(axis=1)
robust = int((ever[TAGS[0.35]] == "alert").sum())

print(f"(admin × season) cells ever flagged alert: {len(ever)}")
print(f"  robust core (alert even at r ≥ 0.35): {robust}")
print(f"  threshold-sensitive:                   {len(ever) - robust}")
ever.n_thresh_alert.value_counts().sort_index().rename("n_alerts").to_frame()
```

About 85 alerts fire at all four thresholds — a high-confidence core. The handful
firing at only one cutoff are the most likely to be noise.

## What relaxing the gate surfaces

The interesting cases appear only once the gate relaxes. Are they credible signal,
or noise we were right to exclude?

```{python}
#| label: tbl-surfaced
d20 = adm0[0.20].set_index(KEY)
d35 = adm0[0.35].set_index(KEY)
surfaced = d20[(d20.tier == "alert") &
               (d35.reindex(d20.index).state != "evaluable")]
print(f"alerts at r=0.20 not even evaluable at r=0.35: {len(surfaced)}")
surfaced.sort_values("z")[["z", "dry_rp", "cov_combined", "dry_frac_footprint"]].head(15)
```

Several are severe and near-total in extent (e.g. **Sudan JJA, z ≈ −3.6, ~93%
dry**), extending the robust East-Africa / Sahel cluster. That tells us a strict
gate causes **misses**, not just guards against false alarms — and for early
warning, a miss is the costlier error. The next chapter turns this into a decision.
